title: Portfolio Pricing Memorandum for the Workplace Cafe Management Program
content:
The management fee a client pays on each cafe contract under the Workplace Cafe Management Program is discounted by a portfolio band that reads the client's whole cafe portfolio rather than the single contract being invoiced — that clause is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis for setting the management fee.

The method by which that band was formerly found is likewise **no longer in force** and superseded by the current basis: it counted the client's cafe contracts standing active or suspended on the day the invoice was raised, then took the highest ladder step whose contract count did not exceed that number, using the ladder printed against the service model of the contract being invoiced, so that two contracts of differing service models in the same portfolio could take different discount percentages from the same count. No figure of the current basis is given here.

**Clauses that remain in force.**

- A portfolio discount, where one applies to a fee element, is applied to the management fee charge only; opening project fees, administration fees, contractual charges and food cost carry no portfolio discount.
- Contracts still in proposal or mobilizing, and contracts already closed, are outside the portfolio count, and a contract in transition out is outside it as well.
- Where the portfolio count changes part way through a billing period, the count taken on the invoice day governs the whole of that invoice, and no retrospective adjustment is made to invoices already raised.

The portfolio discount ladder and the base management fee that the band would apply to remain those printed against the service model of the contract being invoiced, and stay valid entries against each service model even though the clause assembling them is superseded.

superseded_clauses: The band is found by counting the client's cafe contracts that stand active or suspended on the day the invoice is raised, then taking the highest ladder step whose contract count does not exceed that number; the ladder is the one printed against the service model of the contract being invoiced, so two contracts of different service models in the same portfolio take different discount percentages from the same count.
The management fee a client pays on each cafe contract is discounted by a portfolio band that reads the client's whole cafe portfolio rather than the single contract being invoiced.
